name: 172. A provider refusing a direct key returns its own error whatever max_retries is (direct-key-refusal)
description:
A direct key (x-bf-direct-key: true plus the caller's own provider key, enabled by client.allow_direct_keys) is a one-key pool. When the provider refused it and the provider's max_retries left a retry in the budget, the dead pool collapsed into 502 upstream_credentials_exhausted, which tells the caller the gateway's keys ran out and invites a retry with the same bad key. A refused direct key now returns the provider's own error whatever max_retries is; a configured key pinned within the budget still collapses into the 502.

The row creates a run-scoped OpenAI-backed custom provider with max_retries 1 and no keys, sends a chat completion with a throwaway direct key, and requires OpenAI's own 401 with a single attempt in the log row's attempt trail, then deletes the provider. Free: OpenAI rejects the key before any tokens.

Rows 2 to 4 run the same refusal on each drop-in route, with the caller's key in that route's own header: /openai/v1/chat/completions (Authorization) and /anthropic/v1/messages (x-api-key) answer with the provider's own 401, /genai generateContent (x-goog-api-key) with Gemini's own 4xx; streamed, the refusal arrives as an HTTP error before any event. With a fallback in the body, a run-scoped OpenAI-backed provider serves on its gateway key, streamed or not: the caller's key goes to the first route only. Each of rows 2 to 4 then sends the runner's working key for that provider (openaiKey, anthropicKey, genaiKey), streamed and not, and requires a 200 from the route's provider on the caller's key. Run with FEATURE="direct-key-refusal".
